featured_reviews.name: Kinjal Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience at Impulse Studio. I paid for a trial Zumba class scheduled at 10:00 AM. When I arrived, there was no teacher and no students present. The person at reception mentioned that the class usually starts at 10:15, which was different from the time communicated to me.

When I contacted Bosky to clarify, instead of addressing the confusion politely, she was extremely aggressive and rude. I simply mentioned that it was 10:05 AM and no one was there.

As a client-facing business in the fitness industry, basic courtesy and professionalism are expected.

Very disappointed with how this was handled.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
We’re genuinely sorry that your experience didn’t match your expectations—but a little perspective might help balance the narrative.
At 10:02 AM—barely two minutes past the scheduled time—we received a rather urgent demand for a refund, despite the session being clearly non-refundable. In a city like Mumbai, where even trains allow for a minute’s grace before declaring a delay, expecting a full class to be in motion at the exact second is, perhaps, a touch optimistic.
Our class began at 10:15 AM, which is well within the natural rhythm of how group sessions ease into momentum. Fitness, after all, is not instant noodles—it requires a little patience before the magic begins.
Despite this, we still chose to refund your amount as a gesture of goodwill, not obligation—simply to ensure there was no lingering unpleasantness. Ironically, that courtesy seems to have gone unacknowledged.
As for the interaction with Bosky, we did review the exchange. While we always stand for professionalism, we also believe respect is a two-way street. Conversations, much like workouts, tend to go better when they don’t begin at full intensity.
Impulse Studio isn’t built for hurried check-ins and stopwatch exits—it’s built for people who value the process, the energy, and the experience of showing up for themselves.
That said, we sincerely wish you the best in your fitness journey—and perhaps, along the way, the discovery that the first step to fitness isn’t speed, but composure.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Holi, a festival of colours. to celebrate love, community and arrival of spring, PHAGUN as we know in Hindi.
While the entire country rejoiced it with wet and dry colours and water, we celebrated it yesterday at Natanam with the colours of classical music and dance - ‘Baithak’ A mesmerising evening, started with a resounding Pakhwanj recital by Pranay Sakpal and Arjun Shinde, disciples of Shri Sukhad Mundeji, setting the mood and creating a platitude atmosphere.

For the first time I heard Khayal and Thumris renditions by Jayanti Nayak ma’am while our Kathak Sir Prakash Raj emoting it with amazing expressions. They were accompanied by Vaibhav Mankad on harmonium and Kaushik Basu on tabla.

Guru Shubhada with her disciples Mitali and Shreya displayed  the naughtiness of Krishna, the spiritual form of Shiva through Odissi dance form.

This was followed by a  Bharatnatyam performance my Guru Nilesh Singha. His performance started with a recital spreading the message of universal brotherhood - “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam”, the world is one family.
He performed an Ashtapadi which is a Divine Romance between Shree Krisha and Radha celebrating the augmentation of Vasant.

The show ended with a finale by junior and senior kathak students who danced on the phagun songs. Both the Kathak compositions were wrtitten by Padmashri Dr Puru Dadheech, Piyush Sir’s Guru.

Had it not been for Natanam, I wouldn’t have got a chance to witness such amazing performances by these senior artists.
I am surely looking forward to learn my dance form and perform soon. Thank you  Natanam for taking this initiative of Baithak.
